title: Mapping the Infodemic: Geolocating Reddit Users and Unsupervised Topic Modeling of COVID-19-Related Misinformation
screen_reason: The study hand-labels a corpus of geolocated Reddit COVID-19/vaccine comments as true or false and reports the counts of each (3,439 true, 1,575 false out of 5,014), i.e. a share of items in a sample classified false with an explicit denominator = CONTENT. The topic-modeling and geolocation machinery is descriptive, not a classifier-detection paper: the veracity labels are human, and the prevalence counts are stated.

estimates.measure_type: % of geolocated COVID-19/vaccine Reddit comments manually labelled false
estimates.denominator: 5,014 hand-labelled Reddit comments — the subset of ~17.7 million keyword-matched COVID-19/vaccine comments (Dec 2020-Jul 2022) whose authors could be geolocated to a US city/county subreddit (5,853 data points) and that survived preprocessing
estimates.definition: A comment was labelled 'false' by a team of four researchers reviewing 'the context, mood, and overall message to determine its accuracy'
estimates.misinfo_def: The World Health Organization (WHO) called this an “infodemic,” which means that there is too much information, some of which is true and some of which is not, which makes it hard for people to find reliable sources and advice
estimates.source_quote: After filtering, we assembled a final dataset of 5014 labeled Reddit data comments, with 3439 labeled as true and 1575 as false.
estimates.page_loc: Section 3.3 Phase 3: Data Preprocessing and Labeling, p. 5 (Information 2025, 16, 748)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Manual binary true/false labelling by a team of four researchers judging 'the context, mood, and overall message'; inter-annotator agreement Cohen's κ = 0.82. No published codebook, no external fact-check source, no adjudication procedure described.
estimates.moderator_quote: For this study, we collected a total of 17,748,278 Reddit data points. To gather these Reddit data, we used keywords from previous studies on COVID-19 misinformation, such as “vaccine,” “booster,” “unvaccinated,” “Pfizer,” “Moderna,” “5G,” “tower,” “chips,” “microchips,” “Coronavirus,” “COVID19,” “Corona,” “Covid,” and “pandemic”
estimates.notes: Percentage is not printed by the authors; it is an exact part/whole from the two verbatim counts with the same denominator (1575/5014 = 31.41%), permitted under R8. Denominator is NOT a random sample of the 17.7M keyword-matched comments: it is the ~0.03% of comments whose authors always posted in a location-specific subreddit, a strong and undocumented selection, so the value should not be read as the prevalence of misinformation on Reddit at large. JUDGEMENT CALL for the adjudicator: the labelling instruction ('context, mood, and overall message') is looser than a truth judgement, and the paper reports that 67.26% of the humour/sarcasm topic ('jokes about microchips') was labelled FALSE, which suggests jokes about conspiracy claims were coded as misinformation — arguably inflating the false share. Data window Dec 2020-Jul 2022; year set to 2021 as the representative midpoint. topic coded 'vaccines' (COVID-19 vaccination is the stated focus) though the keyword set also spans COVID-19 generally.

missed_or_uncertain: Per-topic FALSE shares are reported for the unsupervised topic clusters: LDA Topic 3 '70.97% FALSE', Topic 0 '(67.26%)', Topic 2 '(60.49%)'; NMF Topic 3 '58% FALSE' and Topic 1 '(57.50% FALSE)'. These are subgroup breakdowns of the same 5,014-comment corpus by machine-derived topic, not separate populations, and the paper gives no per-topic denominators; per the collapse rule (keep the main figure rather than subgroups) they were not extracted. Figure 3 ('Percentage of false news in each county') and Figure 2 (county vaccination rates) are choropleth maps with no numeric county values in the text — only named exemplar counties (Ada, Newton, Flathead, Cloud vs Multnomah, DC, New Castle) with no percentages. The intermediate 5,853 geolocated data points were labelled before preprocessing; only the post-filter 5,014 has a true/false split.

rob.design: Observational content analysis. 17,748,278 Reddit comments collected December 2020-July 2022 via a 14-term COVID-19/vaccine keyword dictionary drawn from prior studies; users geolocated by exclusive participation in city/county subreddits matched to a SimpleMaps city/county list, yielding 5,853 data points; all 5,853 manually labelled true/false by four researchers; unrelated comments and links removed, leaving 5,014 labelled comments (3,439 true, 1,575 false); inter-annotator agreement Cohen's κ = 0.82 reported (unit of agreement and number double-coded not specified). No probability sampling, no codebook, no confidence intervals; authors acknowledge that subreddit-based geolocation may misassign users and that manual labelling is subjective.
rob.item6_quote: In the data labeling process, the 5853 comments were manually labeled as either “true” or “false” by a team of four researchers. We reviewed and evaluated each comment, focusing on the context, mood, and overall message to determine its accuracy.
rob.item10_quote: After filtering, we assembled a final dataset of 5014 labeled Reddit data comments, with 3439 labeled as true and 1575 as false.
